chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram removing ticks from the camel. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and he cannot remove the halamah (the lump of flesh at the base of the horn).'.

key_terms.الْحَلَمَةَ: The halamah (a lump of flesh at the base of the horn, which should not be removed by the one in Ihram)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يُقَرِّدُ: He removes (specifically referring to removing ticks or lice)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on removing ticks from a camel while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of a pilgrim in Ihram removing camel ticks, a common practical concern in the harsh desert environment of the Hijaz. The specific prohibition against removing the 'halamah' (a fleshy protuberance at the base of the horn) highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the animal's natural integrity unless necessary, distinguishing between mere grooming and altering the creature's form. This ruling underscores the balance between ease in worship and respect for creation, a key theme in Shia fiqh regarding Ihram restrictions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam removing ticks from the camel. Heasws said: ‘Yes, and he cannot remove الْحَلَمَةَ’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in the state of Ihram removes ticks from the camel. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is permissible but he must not remove al-Halamah.’”
